title: VPAT readiness: harmonize keyboard affordances and contrast tokens for floating actions, nested tables, and micro-charts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: During the preliminary VPAT assessment for the 2026 design system release we identified inconsistent keyboard affordances and contrast deltas in three component groups: floating action sets (FAB groups and quick-action pills), nested table headers (multi-row headers with inline controls), and micro-charts used in dense dashboards. These inconsistencies cause failures in keyboard-only workflows and produce contrast deltas that fail WCAG AA in some high-density themes.

Goal: Produce a targeted accessibility remediation that: (1) standardizes focus rings and keyboard traversal rules for floating actions and nested table headers; (2) remaps semantic roles and ARIA attributes for nested header controls to ensure screen reader clarity; (3) unify contrast token mappings for micro-charts and action pills so all theme ramps meet WCAG AA; (4) produce VPAT evidence and automated a11y tests for the affected components.

Scope: Design tokens (focus/outline/hover), floating-action components (FAB group, quick-action pill, action overflow), table header variants (simple, grouped, virtualized), and micro-chart legends/tooltips. Excludes full data-visual overhaul — only style/accessibility layer changes.

Deliverables: Design spec with keyboard matrix and focus examples, updated token mapping document, Figma file with annotated components, a short developer guide for required ARIA changes, acceptance-test checklist for QA engineers, VPAT annex pages for the affected components, and PR reviews for two implementation branches.

Success metrics: All mapped components pass axe-core baseline and manual keyboard + VoiceOver checks; VPAT annex shows resolved issues for keyboard navigation and contrast; developer friction reduced (clear implementation guide and tiny token deltas).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Keyboard tab order defined and documented for FAB groups and nested headers; 2) Focus styles applied via tokens and visible at 3:1 contrast ratio in compact themes, 4:1 in default themes; 3) ARIA role/value changes applied and validated in screen reader walkthroughs (VoiceOver + NVDA); 4) Micro-chart color tokens updated and verified against theme permutations; 5) Automated tests added to design-system storybook that assert focusable order and contrast; 6) VPAT annex pages drafted and attached to the release package.
comments: 2026-01-16 — Kickoff meeting: aligned on scope, invited ENG owners (ENG-5123) and PM triage (PM-234). Agreed to keep implementation non-breaking; aim for tokens-only where possible. — Asha

2026-01-21 — Design work in progress: created keyboard traversal matrix and two focus treatments (thin high-contrast ring vs. filled focus slab). Shared Figma file: https://figma.redwood/design-system/a11y-fab-headers (permission: team). — Marco

2026-01-26 — Engineering spike results: ENG verified that token swap approach works for FAB groups and micro-charts; nested table headers require a small DOM structure change to ensure logical tab stops. Raised ENG PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/2781 — Priya (ENG)

2026-01-30 — Accessibility review with external consultant: recommended changing role="button" on inline controls to role="menuitemcheckbox" in grouped headers for clearer state announcement. Also recommended contrast ramp update for the medium theme. Documented in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/inclusive/design-vpat-2026#deltas — Asha

2026-02-01 — QA run: axe baseline passed for FAB group and micro-charts in default theme; nested headers flagged for tabindex issues in virtualized table story. Filed ENG follow-up ticket ENG-5172 for virtualization fix. — QA Team
2026-02-02 — Submitted VPAT annex draft and attached test artifacts to the release package. Marking ticket In Review and requesting design sign-off from Accessibility PM before merge. — Marco
